answer.summary: For customer and market research in product ops, Melissa Perri recommends someone with user-research (ideally research-ops and possibly UX) experience, strong research methods, and an operational mindset: someone who can build systems and toolkits that make research more effective and scalable.

sections.heading: Recommended background and strengths
sections.content: Look for someone with a user research background, potentially UX experience; a strong research-ops background is especially valuable. They should understand good research tactics and interviewing, and be able to create research toolkits and select appropriate prototyping and usability software. Perri emphasizes a process-oriented person who wants to improve things and can operationalize work by building systems.

sections.heading: What that looks like in practice
sections.content: Research operations can include building a participant database and research toolkits, overseeing research tools, and training others to conduct good research. Perri describes a system that certifies people to do research at different levels where compliance requires it, with user researchers stepping in when a study raises compliance issues. More broadly, the product-ops role streamlines and enables research—it does not replace the people conducting it.
